key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly tune nickelate defects and electronic states, improving oxygen evolution activity while enhancing structural durability relative to LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: Combining compositional disorder with epitaxial strain offers a route to engineer more active, degradation-resistant perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Characterize structural faults, Ni valence, electronic states, and electrochemical OER response.
Use first-principles calculations to interpret strain-dependent rare-earth orbital hybridization.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy material better resists structural degradation than LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and transferability from epitaxial films to practical catalyst architectures remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
